title: Face with Symbols on Mouth Emoji 🤬 Meaning: Cursing
description: The 🤬 emoji shows a red face with censor symbols over its mouth. It means swearing with rage or frustration. See when it is funny and when it goes too far.
summary: The 🤬 face with symbols on mouth is a red, furious face whose mouth is covered by a bar of characters like @#$%&!. It means the sender is so angry they are cursing, with the actual words bleeped out. It is the most intense anger emoji, and often a comic one.
meaning: Comic strips have long replaced swear words with strings of typographic symbols, a device cartoonists call a grawlix. This emoji puts that device on a face. The result is a way to swear without swearing: the reader understands that profanity is happening and fills in the words themselves. Nothing rude is actually written, which is the appeal.

It sits at the top of the anger scale. Where 😠 is annoyed and 😡 is furious, 🤬 has lost control. People use it for the kind of frustration that makes them shout at a screen: a deleted file, a last-second loss, stepping on a toy barefoot, an hour on hold followed by a dropped call.

Its cartoon origins keep it from feeling as threatening as it looks. Much of the time it is venting with a wink, and the censor bar itself is funny. It also serves as a stand-in for a specific curse word in sentences, as in “what the 🤬,” and as a label warning that strong language follows. Added in 2017, it is now a standard part of gaming and sports trash talk.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It punctuates stories about infuriating events: “the airline lost my bag AGAIN 🤬.” The anger is usually aimed at circumstances, not at the reader. When it is aimed at the reader, it is the emoji equivalent of yelling and should be taken as a sign that the person is extremely upset.

contexts.label: In gaming and sports
contexts.body: Players send it after cheap deaths, lag, and teammates who throw a match. Fans use it for blown leads and bad officiating. In these settings it is expected and rarely taken personally. It also substitutes for profanity in chats with language filters.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It shows up in rants about customer service, traffic, politics and technology failures. Creators use it in titles to suggest an angry or explicit reaction while staying within platform rules on language. Used at another user, it is hostile and can escalate an argument quickly.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It implies profanity, so treat it like profanity. In a close-knit team it might get a laugh after a server outage. In most workplaces, and always with clients or managers, it is out of place. A sentence describing what went wrong does the job without the risk.

examples.text: Laptop crashed and I hadn't saved in two hours 🤬
examples.meaning: Swearing-level frustration at a painful loss of work.

examples.text: What the 🤬 was that call, ref?
examples.meaning: The emoji replaces a curse word in the sentence.

examples.text: Stubbed my toe on the same table leg again 🤬
examples.meaning: Comic rage at a small, painful mishap.

examples.text: He lied to my face for six months 🤬
Lost the match because of lag 🤬🤬
examples.meaning: A gamer venting about something outside their control.

combos.meaning: Fury that has tipped over into cursing.
Rage at a video game; close to rage-quitting.
So angry the sender's head is about to explode.
Infuriated by a phone call, typically with customer service.

confusedWith.difference: 😡 is a red scowl with nothing over its mouth: intense but silent anger. 🤬 adds the censor bar, which specifically means swearing and pushes the intensity higher.
🤐 has a zipper for a mouth and means keeping a secret or staying quiet. 🤬 also has a covered mouth, but the symbols show words pouring out, not being held in.
👿 is a purple, horned scowl suggesting malice or a devilish grudge. 🤬 is a human outburst of temper with no sinister undertone.

avoid: Do not aim it at a person unless you are prepared for the conversation to become a fight.
Avoid it in professional or customer-facing messages.
Skip it around people who object to swearing, since it stands for the words even though it hides them.
design: A red or orange-red face with angry, slanted eyebrows and a black or dark bar across the mouth filled with white symbols such as @, #, $, %, & and !. Each vendor chooses a slightly different set and order of symbols. The red face and censor bar are constant, though some designs glare with wide eyes and others squint.

faqs.q: What do the symbols on 🤬 mean?
faqs.a: They stand for swear words. Using characters like @#$%! in place of profanity is an old comic-strip technique known as a grawlix. The symbols have no individual meanings; together they signal censored cursing.

faqs.q: Is 🤬 a bad emoji to send?
faqs.a: It is not obscene in itself, but it implies obscenity and strong anger. Among friends it is usually humorous venting. Directed at someone, or used in a formal setting, it is rude.

faqs.q: What does 🤬 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: The meaning does not change by gender: the person is extremely frustrated or angry. Check whether the target is a situation, like traffic or a game, or you. The first is venting; the second needs to be addressed.
😡 is furious. 🤬 is furious and swearing about it. The swearing face is one notch stronger and also a little more cartoonish, which is why it is often used for comic effect.

faqs.q: When was the cursing emoji added?
faqs.a: It was approved in Unicode 10.0 in 2017, in the same release as the exploding head 🤯 and the shushing face 🤫.
